# Eonrise brief

**Question:** why do lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated charging cycles

**Root topic:** lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated

**Status:** usable — 4/5 relations grounded after gap repair

**Evidence:** 37 papers kept of 37 retrieved (24 on topic), 75 concepts

*README.md in this folder says what every file, field and number means.*

## Grounded map

- **Mechanism:** machine learning, home storage
- **Measurement:** soh estimation, mode estimation
- **Failure Mode:** degradation modes, degradation mechanisms, degradation models
- **Method:** not grounded yet
- **Neighbor Field:** energy storage, degradation diagnostics, cycle life prediction

## Stated limitations

- **raising stress** — "Notes that simply raising stress ignores mechanisms, and the same capacity attenuation does not mean the same state of health when mechanisms differ."
- **laboratory data** — "Highlights limitations of laboratory data and reviews practical challenges of field battery data for SoH estimation."

## Same shape, other fields

*These look unrelated on purpose: each solved a problem with the same shape as yours, in another field. Before judging one, write what they solved and what your version would be.*

- **Bayesian and likelihood inferences on remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under gamma process** (2017, Reliability Engineering)
  - What they did: Develops likelihood and Bayesian inference for remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under a gamma process, with a random rate change time.
  - Shared concepts: degradation models
- **A Wiener-process-based degradation model with a recursive filter algorithm for remaining useful life estimation** (2013, Mechanical Systems and Signal Processing)
  - What they did: Uses a recursive filter to update the drift coefficient of a Wiener process and the EM algorithm to update all other parameters whenever new degradation data become available, to estimate remaining useful life.
  - Shared concepts: degradation models

## Concept directions

- **down:** degradation modes, degradation mechanisms, machine learning
- **sideways:** lithium ion batteries, lithium plating, state of health, li ion batteries

**Gaps:** method

**Not in this literature:** method — two full rounds produced no candidate at all, so the run stopped spending queries on it rather than calling it an unfilled gap.

## Next searches

- `lithium ion batteries experiment`
- `lithium ion batteries ablation experiment`

## Searches toward other fields

- `degradation models`

corpus_papers.abstract: Comprehensive review of Li-ion degradation and capacity decline under different cycling conditions. Loss of cyclable lithium often dominates total capacity loss and is typically linked to SEI surface film formation on graphite anodes. Lithium plating occurs with fast charging or low temperature and reacts with electrolyte to form additional SEI.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Degradation in Li-ion batteries and capacity decline under different cycling conditions: A comprehensive review

corpus_papers.abstract: Review of degradation mechanisms in commercial lithium-ion cells. Mechanical loss of active material reduces active surface area, so remaining material carries higher interfacial current density, accelerating SEI growth and particle cracking.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: State-of-the-art review of degradation mechanisms of commercial lithium-ion batteries

corpus_papers.abstract: Uses peak signatures in voltage and capacity differentials with an open-circuit voltage model and optimization routines to quantify degradation modes. IC and DV analyses are effective for monitoring battery health, though diagnosis often requires considerable parameterization effort and low scan rates.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Peak-tracking method to quantify degradation modes in lithium-ion batteries via differential voltage and incremental capacity

corpus_papers.abstract: Quantifies via peak detection how charge/discharge rate affects ICA on two cells. ICA normally needs low constant currents to limit resistance and diffusion effects, which is unfeasible for EV charging. Introduces a faster ICA that corrects peak shift using SOC-dependent resistance from current interrupt. Accuracy of ICA reduces at higher C-rates; C/6 is reported as optimum.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Rate dependency of incremental capacity analysis (dQ/dV) as a diagnostic tool for lithium-ion batteries

corpus_papers.abstract: Decouples LLI and positive-electrode active material loss in normal aging, then combines single accelerated protocols by their mechanism proportions. Notes that simply raising stress ignores mechanisms, and the same capacity attenuation does not mean the same state of health when mechanisms differ. Reports acceleration of 62x and 39x under extreme and gentle conditions.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Accelerated aging protocols design for Li-ion batteries based on equivalence of the degradation mechanisms

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews degradation models for lithium-ion batteries. Major degradation mechanisms include formation and growth of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), lithium plating, and loss of active electrode material. These map onto degradation modes: loss of cyclable lithium, loss of active materials, and loss of electrolyte.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Review of State-of-the-Art Degradation Models for Lithium-Ion Batteries

corpus_papers.abstract: Physics-based single particle model extended with electrolyte dynamics and side reactions to simulate degradation of lithium-ion batteries such as SEI growth and lithium plating.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: A Single Particle Model with Electrolyte and Side Reactions for degradation of lithium-ion batteries

corpus_papers.abstract: Many combinations of degradation mechanisms can produce the same patterns of capacity and power fade, making it impossible to find a unique validated solution from capacity data alone. Three models of differing complexity all fit capacity and resistance well, but only the model with five coupled mechanisms also fit degradation modes at all temperatures. Validating only against capacity and power fade is stated to be no longer sufficient.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: The importance of degradation mode analysis in parameterising lifetime prediction models of lithium-ion battery degradation

corpus_papers.abstract: Predicting lithium-ion battery lifetime is described as one of the greatest unsolved problems in battery research. Most prediction papers validate against remaining capacity, but different mechanism combinations give the same fade, so no unique solution exists. Degradation mode analysis (LLI, LAM at both electrodes, electrode slippage) is proposed as validation.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Lithium-ion battery degradation: using degradation mode analysis to validate lifetime prediction modelling

corpus_papers.abstract: Re-parametrizes a full-cell OCV model by N/P and Li/P ratios and derives gradients of electrode slippage and OCV with respect to LLI and LAM parameters. Characterizes four regimes of degradation identifiability and uses Fisher information to identify informative SOC windows for degradation mode estimation.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Identifiability Study of Lithium-Ion Battery Capacity Fade Using Degradation Mode Sensitivity for a Minimally and Intuitively Parametrized Electrode-Specific Cell Open-Circuit Voltage Model

corpus_papers.abstract: Critical review of pOCV, IC-DV, EIS and differential thermal voltammetry for quantifying conductivity loss, LAM and LLI, focused on strengths and weaknesses for automotive use. BMSs currently do not indicate the underlying degradation modes. Pseudo-OCV and IC-DV are found more advantageous than EIS and DTV.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Critical review of non-invasive diagnosis techniques for quantification of degradation modes in lithium-ion batteries

corpus_papers.abstract: Highlights limitations of laboratory data and reviews practical challenges of field battery data for SoH estimation. Field data quality is far from ideal and incompatible with most state-of-the-art data-driven techniques. Challenges: bridging lab to real conditions, more reliable SoH labeling, less dependence on large training data.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Reviewing Practical Challenges in Estimating the State-of-Health of Lithium-Ion Batteries from Field Battery Data

corpus_papers.abstract: Charging at 20 C and discharging at 40 C replicates normal aging at 25 C with acceleration factor above 5 or even 8. Aims to preserve the aging mechanisms of normal conditions; mechanistic consistency is confirmed with incremental capacity analysis.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: An accelerated aging test procedure for lithium-ion battery based on a dual-temperature approach

corpus_papers.abstract: Frames degradation as depletion of finite interacting reservoirs (lithium, porosity, electrolyte) using a DFN model with SEI growth, lithium plating, cracking and solvent dry-out. Over 1,000 cycles, 1% more electrolyte or 5% more porosity extends life by over 30%; excess lithium can accelerate failure without structural or ionic buffers.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Lithium-ion battery degradation: Introducing the concept of reservoirs to design for lifetime

corpus_papers.abstract: Reconstructs the OCV curve continuously over battery lifetime from eight years of operational data of 21 home storage systems (LMO/NMC blend, NMC, LFP). ICA and DVA are applied for degradation mode estimation. Loss of lithium inventory is dominant, while LAM at negative and positive electrodes may be present in some cases.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Degradation mode estimation using reconstructed open circuit voltage curves from multi-year home storage field data

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews rapid nonlinear degradation ('knees') that severely limits lifetime. Discusses six knee pathways: lithium plating, electrode saturation, resistance growth, electrolyte and additive depletion, percolation-limited connectivity, and mechanical deformation, some with internal state trajectories that are electrochemically undetectable. Notes challenges for knee modeling and prediction.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: "Knees" in lithium-ion battery aging trajectories

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews SoH estimation for real-world EVs. Most work is laboratory-based, leaving a gap to deployment; real batteries face dynamic loads, irregular charging and varied environments. SoH estimation is affected by data heterogeneity, environmental variability and label uncertainty.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: State-of-Health Estimation for Li-Ion Batteries of Real-World Electric Vehicles: Progress, Challenges, and Prospects

corpus_papers.abstract: Examines how changes to neuropsychological test batteries in long-running aging studies affect estimates of cognitive decline. When item response theory scoring is used, changes in test batteries over time may not meaningfully affect estimates of cognitive decline.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Examining the Consequences of Neuropsychological Test Battery Changes on Measuring Cognitive Decline
topic_path: measurement harmonization in cognitive aging studies

corpus_papers.abstract: Builds a macroeconomic model showing that in an economy where capacity is generally in excess, demand shocks can be the main driving forces of business cycles. Capacity is never fully utilized at the aggregate level.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Excess Capacity and Demand-Driven Business Cycles

corpus_papers.abstract: Overview of degradation mechanisms and their cell-level consequences (degradation modes: conductivity loss, loss of active material, loss of lithium inventory). Presents differential curves as non-invasive, straightforward diagnostic and prognostic tools, alongside pOCV, IC-DV, EIS and differential thermal voltammetry.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Degradation mechanisms and differential curve modeling for non-invasive diagnostics of lithium cells: An overview

corpus_papers.abstract: Degradation mode analysis decomposes capacity fade into LLI and LAM from low-rate voltage-capacity data, but the measured trace includes ohmic drop and charge-discharge hysteresis (notably in graphite-silicon oxide). These can create 'Phantom LAM/LLI', apparent material loss produced by curve registration, branch choice and voltage-windowing rather than true degradation. Tested on LG M50T and Molicel P45B cells with an IR correction.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Phantom LAM and LLI: Resistance and Hysteresis Bias in Voltage-Curve Degradation Mode Analysis

corpus_papers.abstract: Generates a dataset of 124 commercial LFP/graphite cells under fast charging with cycle lives from 150 to 2,300. Uses discharge voltage curves from early cycles with machine learning; best models reach 9.1% test error predicting cycle life from the first 100 cycles and 4.9% error classifying from the first 5 cycles. Capacity fade is negligible in the first 100 cycles and alone is not a good predictor.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Data-driven prediction of battery cycle life before capacity degradation

corpus_papers.abstract: Optimizes six-step ten-minute fast-charging protocols for maximum cycle life using an early-outcome predictor and Bayesian optimization. Needed because testing a single cell to failure under fast charging takes about 40 days and many parameters must be optimized.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Closed-loop optimization of fast-charging protocols for batteries with machine learning

corpus_papers.abstract: Presents a computerized working memory test battery for young adults. Paper describes assessment of working memory capacity components.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Working memory test battery for young adults: Computerized working memory assessment

corpus_papers.abstract: Cohort study of long-term lithium therapy (a psychiatric mood stabilizer) and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia. Large-scale epidemiological studies have shown that lithium treatment elevates the risk of chronic kidney disease.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
corpus_papers.title: Long-term lithium therapy and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia: a cohort study

corpus_papers.abstract: Review of health indicators, models and machine learning for SOH estimation. Existing methods are highly data dependent with insufficient physical interpretability and limited cross-scenario generalization; the relation between degradation mechanisms and health indicators is not fully explored.
corpus_papers.title: State of Health Estimation and Battery Management: A Review of Health Indicators, Models and Machine Learning

corpus_papers.abstract: Notes that existing prediction frameworks rely on rigid unchanging protocols that fail to capture real-world dynamics. Combines hidden Markov processes for realistic power simulation, automated batch testing, an XPS-derived interfacial chemistry database and machine learning to predict degradation under randomized conditions.
corpus_papers.title: Chemistry-aware battery degradation prediction under simulated real-world cyclic protocols

corpus_papers.abstract: Develops likelihood and Bayesian inference for remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under a gamma process, with a random rate change time. Gamma processes model monotone degradation data.
corpus_papers.title: Bayesian and likelihood inferences on remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under gamma process

corpus_papers.abstract: Estimates remaining useful lifetime when the gamma deterioration process is observed with noise (measurement error).
corpus_papers.title: Remaining useful lifetime estimation and noisy gamma deterioration process

corpus_papers.abstract: Develops a gamma-process model for bivariate dependent degradation data, where dependency between the two degradation processes is captured by a common random effect, and applies it to remaining useful life prediction.
corpus_papers.title: A common random effect induced bivariate gamma degradation process with application to remaining useful life prediction

corpus_papers.abstract: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for a gamma degradation process, updating the posterior as new degradation data arrive.
corpus_papers.title: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for gamma degradation process

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews Wiener-process-based methods for degradation data analysis and RUL estimation. Advantages: degradation paths need not be strictly monotonic under noise, and first-hitting-time gives closed-form failure time expressions.
corpus_papers.title: Degradation data analysis and remaining useful life estimation: A review on Wiener-process-based methods

corpus_papers.abstract: Uses a recursive filter to update the drift coefficient of a Wiener process and the EM algorithm to update all other parameters whenever new degradation data become available, to estimate remaining useful life.
corpus_papers.title: A Wiener-process-based degradation model with a recursive filter algorithm for remaining useful life estimation

corpus_papers.abstract: Review of kidney toxicity of lithium in patients treated for bipolar disorder. Lithium enters collecting duct principal cells via the epithelial sodium channel and disrupts vasopressin-regulated water handling by downregulating aquaporin-2.
corpus_papers.title: Lithium nephrotoxicity

corpus_papers.abstract: Reviews renal mechanisms and nephrotoxicity phenotypes of lithium in bipolar disorder. Risk is amplified by episodes of lithium intoxication, dehydration, interacting medications, longer treatment duration and comorbid kidney disease.
corpus_papers.title: Lithium in Bipolar Disorder: Renal Mechanisms, Nephrotoxicity Phenotypes, and a Shared-Care Pathway for Clinical Practice

corpus_papers.abstract: Studies renal function in patients on long-term lithium treatment for bipolar disorder using novel biomarkers.
corpus_papers.title: Impact of Long-Term Lithium Treatment on Renal Function in Patients With Bipolar Disorder Based on Novel Biomarkers

corpus_papers.abstract: Epidemiological study of lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia in Japan. Reviews describe such epidemiological studies as inconclusive because of indirect evidence.
corpus_papers.title: Lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia: Epidemiological Findings from National Data Base of Japan

Field data quality is far from ideal and incompatible with most state-of-the-art data-driven techniques. Challenges: bridging lab to real conditions, more reliable SoH labeling, less dependence on large training data.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
papers.title: Reviewing Practical Challenges in Estimating the State-of-Health of Lithium-Ion Batteries from Field Battery Data

papers.abstract: Examines how changes to neuropsychological test batteries in long-running aging studies affect estimates of cognitive decline. When item response theory scoring is used, changes in test batteries over time may not meaningfully affect estimates of cognitive decline.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
papers.title: Examining the Consequences of Neuropsychological Test Battery Changes on Measuring Cognitive Decline
topic_path: measurement harmonization in cognitive aging studies

papers.abstract: Cohort study of long-term lithium therapy (a psychiatric mood stabilizer) and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia. Large-scale epidemiological studies have shown that lithium treatment elevates the risk of chronic kidney disease.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
papers.title: Long-term lithium therapy and risk of chronic kidney disease, hyperparathyroidism and hypercalcemia: a cohort study

papers.abstract: Develops a gamma-process model for bivariate dependent degradation data, where dependency between the two degradation processes is captured by a common random effect, and applies it to remaining useful life prediction.
papers.title: A common random effect induced bivariate gamma degradation process with application to remaining useful life prediction

papers.abstract: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for a gamma degradation process, updating the posterior as new degradation data arrive.
papers.title: Online Bayesian prediction of remaining useful life for gamma degradation process

papers.abstract: Epidemiological study of lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia in Japan. Reviews describe such epidemiological studies as inconclusive because of indirect evidence.
papers.title: Lithium in drinking water and Alzheimer's dementia: Epidemiological Findings from National Data Base of Japan

papers.abstract: Studies renal function in patients on long-term lithium treatment for bipolar disorder using novel biomarkers.
papers.title: Impact of Long-Term Lithium Treatment on Renal Function in Patients With Bipolar Disorder Based on Novel Biomarkers

papers.abstract: Reviews Wiener-process-based methods for degradation data analysis and RUL estimation. Advantages: degradation paths need not be strictly monotonic under noise, and first-hitting-time gives closed-form failure time expressions.
papers.title: Degradation data analysis and remaining useful life estimation: A review on Wiener-process-based methods

papers.abstract: Presents a computerized working memory test battery for young adults. Paper describes assessment of working memory capacity components.
found_by: lithium-ion batteries lose capacity over repeated
papers.title: Working memory test battery for young adults: Computerized working memory assessment

papers.abstract: Develops likelihood and Bayesian inference for remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under a gamma process, with a random rate change time. Gamma processes model monotone degradation data.
papers.title: Bayesian and likelihood inferences on remaining useful life in two-phase degradation models under gamma process

papers.abstract: Estimates remaining useful lifetime when the gamma deterioration process is observed with noise (measurement error).
papers.title: Remaining useful lifetime estimation and noisy gamma deterioration process

papers.abstract: Review of kidney toxicity of lithium in patients treated for bipolar disorder. Lithium enters collecting duct principal cells via the epithelial sodium channel and disrupts vasopressin-regulated water handling by downregulating aquaporin-2.
papers.title: Lithium nephrotoxicity

papers.abstract: Uses a recursive filter to update the drift coefficient of a Wiener process and the EM algorithm to update all other parameters whenever new degradation data become available, to estimate remaining useful life.
papers.title: A Wiener-process-based degradation model with a recursive filter algorithm for remaining useful life estimation

papers.abstract: Reviews renal mechanisms and nephrotoxicity phenotypes of lithium in bipolar disorder. Risk is amplified by episodes of lithium intoxication, dehydration, interacting medications, longer treatment duration and comorbid kidney disease.
papers.title: Lithium in Bipolar Disorder: Renal Mechanisms, Nephrotoxicity Phenotypes, and a Shared-Care Pathway for Clinical Practice
